title: Hydrocarbons
seo_title: Hydrocarbons Class 11 Chemistry Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 9)
standard_text: Classification of hydrocarbons. Aliphatic hydrocarbons: alkanes – nomenclature, isomerism, conformation (ethane only), physical properties, chemical reactions; alkenes – nomenclature, structure of double bond, geometrical isomerism, methods of preparation, chemical reactions: addition of hydrogen, halogen, water, hydrogen halides (Markovnikov's addition and peroxide effect), ozonolysis, oxidation, mechanism of electrophilic addition; alkynes – nomenclature, structure of triple bond, methods of preparation, chemical reactions, acidic character of alkynes. Aromatic hydrocarbons: introduction, IUPAC nomenclature, benzene: resonance, aromaticity, chemical properties, mechanism of electrophilic substitution, directive influence of a functional group in monosubstituted benzene. Carcinogenicity and toxicity.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 11 Chemistry worksheets for NCERT Chapter 9 Hydrocarbons: alkanes, alkenes and alkynes, formulae, combustion, Wurtz reaction, Markovnikov's rule, benzene and electrophilic substitution. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Alkanes CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, alkenes CₙH₂ₙ, alkynes CₙH₂ₙ₋₂.
body_html:
How to think about it

Alkanes (CnH2n+2) are saturated and react by free-radical substitution. Alkenes (CnH2n) and alkynes (CnH2n−2) are unsaturated and take part in addition reactions; HX adds by Markovnikov's rule, except HBr with peroxide. The Wurtz reaction joins two alkyl groups with sodium.

Benzene has 6 delocalised π electrons and is aromatic by Hückel's (4n + 2) rule, so it prefers electrophilic substitution such as nitration and Friedel–Crafts reactions. Groups such as –OH and –CH₃ direct new groups to ortho and para positions; –NO₂ directs to meta.

Example

Alkyne with 4 carbons?

CₙH₂ₙ₋₂

Answer: C₄H₆

Example

HBr + propene?

Markovnikov

Answer: 2-bromopropane

Common mistakes

  • Writing alkynes as CₙH₂ₙ.
  • Forgetting the peroxide effect for HBr.
  • Saying benzene adds bromine easily like an alkene.

faq.a: When HX adds to an unsymmetrical alkene, the hydrogen goes to the carbon that already has more hydrogen atoms.

faq.q: Why does benzene undergo substitution rather than addition?
faq.a: Substitution keeps the stable aromatic π system; addition would destroy it.
